I'll do my best. I've played with it a little and got it running. Newer browser based technologies like webtorrent and peer to peer streams allow users to transfer data directly between each other without going through an extra hop to a central server. These central servers are usually what host sites like voat. When you see voat down from too many people hitting it at once, it's because the central server is choking. Zeronet is a software you install that runs and allows you to access and host sites directly from your computer. You access zeronet sites through a browser the same way you normally do. Much like torrents, sites on zeronet are hosted by everyone on zeronet. So instead of everyone trying to hit one server, everyone is loading the site from everyone else.

Zeronet cleverly uses the bitcoin blockchain as a way to host addresses. It's anonymous in the sense that you can't link an IP address to a person. But the more security-minded folks should use a VPN or TOR for anonymity. In the future, I'd like to see the software that runs zeronet in browser-based plugins for chrome and firefox.

With the NFL having a new agreement with Tottenham to play NFL games there over the next several years, it seems that the NFL is still pushing for a larger international audience. For the last couple years, we've seen owners and sometimes league officials comment (albeit anonymously in the latter's case) about a permanent team in London. Though the NFL hasn't been back recently, the Card and Niners played out in Mexico City and it was a huge sellout. Toronto, as we all know, hosted the Bills.

So I ask you, voat NFLers, how do you feel about the NFL's international push? Do you think the NFL puts a team in another country in the next 10-15 years? Where?
USA NFL Fans, how do you feel about the NFL on an international level?
I just wanna say anyone who thinks the Toronto series is a good example of judging how much Canadians like football don't understand anything about how much we love our sports
I hope Canada can get their own team in some way. Personally I think the divisions are perfect as is, but Canada and Mexico are who the NFL should be focusing on.

I like the divisions, and while most people might not like it, it made a lot of sense for the Bills to move to Toronto, nothing would've changed for divisions

I personally would love if somehow we ended up with the Toronto Raiders or something though

I don't think an NFL team will be sustainable overseas.

And I hope we don't try to put one there.

No offense to overseas fans, but the push for broader appeal is ruining football. Players lose rest and prep time in overseas games. Teams lose the advantage of a home crowd.

Its a sideshow. All I ever hear about overseas games is that the majority of fans in the seats are rooting for the kickers and punters.

It's not legitimate.

The NFL wants to pull as many casual fans as possible and its hurting their image.

Football is chess yet everyone thinks of it as barbarians or even worse fat barbarians. People don't realize the level of athleticism or the amount of thinking that goes on in football. Name an offensive lineman he can probably out run you. He definitely understands very complicated concepts about how to scheme to block defenses.

Football should sell itself. There's nothing like being at a close game in the 4th quarter when everyone is on their feet watching what is going to happen next, and the desire to bring in casual fans has killed that moment. Everybody sits and nobody thinks and its all lost on them.

There has to be a better way to share the game I love than the way the NFL is going about it.

Personally, I think if the NFL wants to play games in other countries, those countries should have an NFL team. Without that, I feel like it's just a money-grab attempt, and slighting the teams city, and don't approve.

I think that Europe is a horrible idea, hope it never happens on a permanent basis. Especially if there was only one team in Europe and other teams were forced to travel there every year. Canada and Mexico makes some sense, but I think in general the international games only do well because they are a novelty.

I honestly have no problems with it. Most teams show up anywhere from two to three days before the game to practice anyways so why would it change going to another country. I am sure the NFL would put a team on a bye after playing in another country or continent.
Olympics, sure. Average season, no no no no no. However, despite my (and most of NFL viewers) viewpoints, I'm sure Britain will have a NFL team in the next 10-15 years.

I would love to see international teams in the NFL. London, Mexico, Canada, Brazil anywhere where it is popular. Soccer over there have multiple countries in one league. It would get our sport in new markets. If the NFL is the best in the world we'll need to play the world.

I honestly dont think we should put another team in another country. If anything, the rest of the world needs to catch up to the NFL. Even if it takes years, get that started. I would love a World Cup of Football (not futbol). I know thats a long shot but as a fan, I would love that.

I think an expansion to Europe is a bad idea, though it might be a good idea to invest in a European League (like a cross Europe single league) and we could play like exhibition games in the offseason, or the different league championship winners play each other. Try and get it up to Canada's level of play and popularity. However, across the border to Mexico City could work, but I don't think its the best idea

I'd love to see a European (just as an example) league take off, but would absolutely not welcome a Euro team into the NA league. The travel times along would completely fuck the teams involved. It's just not reasonable.

That said, I'd be all for North American teams outside of the US joining in!

American Football is the One True Sport but the dynamics of a world league is going to be difficult. I think the NFL should just help develop leagues on other continents until they are on par with itself and then have some kind of world championship. Soccer is only so popular because the poor and uneducated masses of the world have been denied the spectacle that is American Football. This comment is only partially tongue in cheek.

I don't mind the push for international appeal, as they want to grow the brand and hopefully start producing talent elsewhere. However, I strongly am against moving a team overseas. The travel time is just too big a hurdle. The only way they could put a team outside of America is in Canada or Mexico City. Honestly I would love a team in Mexico City, The appeal is there and they wouldn't have a big problem gaining support.
I think the major hangup for a European team is the lack of a supersonic commercial jet. Without one the flights are just too long to seriously consider having a permanent team in London.
